Locally ringed space

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Geometry and topology Algebraic geometry Ringed space
OurBigBook.com Words: 9k Articles: 190
A locally ringed space is a ringed space whose stalk OX,x​ is a local ring at every point. Morphisms of locally ringed spaces induce local homomorphisms on stalks.

Morphism of locally ringed spaces (fx#​:OY,f(x)​→OX,x​)

Words: 33
Locally ringed space OurBigBook.com
A morphism is a continuous map f:X→Y together with a homomorphism OY​→f∗​OX​ of sheaves of rings whose induced map on every stalk is a local homomorphism. Applied to schemes, this is exactly a morphism of schemes.

Scheme

Words: 9k Articles: 188
Locally ringed space OurBigBook.com
A scheme is a locally ringed space covered by open subsets isomorphic to spectra of commutative rings. It retains both the points defined by prime ideals and the local algebra of functions around them.

Schemes are Kolmogorov spaces

Words: 62
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The underlying topological space of every scheme is a Kolmogorov space: any two distinct points are distinguished by an open subset containing just one. Choose an affine open subscheme containing the first point. If it omits the second, it already distinguishes them. Otherwise, the two points correspond to distinct prime ideals, and an element in one but not the other defines a principal open subscheme distinguishing them. Thus distinct points of a scheme have distinct closures.

Locally Noetherian scheme

Words: 48
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme is locally Noetherian if it has an affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. It is a Noetherian scheme exactly when it is also a quasi-compact scheme: a finite subcover then supplies the required finite affine open cover. An infinite gluing of spectra of Noetherian rings along open subschemes is still locally Noetherian, but need not be a quasi-compact scheme.

Functor represented by a scheme (hX​(R)=Hom(SpecR,X))

Words: 330 Articles: 4
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The functor of points describes a scheme through its morphisms from test schemes. On commutative rings, it is covariant because a ring homomorphism reverses the corresponding affine-scheme map. A functor on rings is represented by X in the algebraic-geometric sense when it is naturally isomorphic to hX​. The representing scheme need not be affine; this is different from demanding a representable functor in the category of rings itself.
// Target: module-theory.bigb

Field-valued points do not detect nilpotents

Words: 60
Functor represented by a scheme OurBigBook.com
Let A be a commutative ring and I an ideal all of whose elements are nilpotent elements. Every ring homomorphism from A to a field kills I, because a field has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Thus the closed immersion Spec(A/I)↪SpecA induces a bijection on points valued in every field, even when it is not an isomorphism of schemes. The dual numbers provide the smallest example. Testing the functor of points on all affine schemes does detect this information, by affine test schemes determine scheme morphisms.

Affine test schemes determine scheme morphisms (Hom(X,Y)≅Nat(gX​,gY​))

Words: 84
Functor represented by a scheme OurBigBook.com
Restricting the functor of points to affine schemes gives a fully faithful functor from schemes to covariant set-valued functors on commutative rings. Given a natural transformation, apply it to the inclusions of an affine open cover of X. Naturality on affine open subschemes of overlaps makes the resulting maps to Y agree, so they glue. For an arbitrary map from an affine scheme to X, cover its inverse images of these charts by affine open subschemes and apply naturality again. This proves that the glued map induces the prescribed natural transformation, and uniqueness follows from the original cover. In particular, the restricted functor of points determines the scheme up to an isomorphism of schemes.

Open affine representability criterion

Words: 72
Functor represented by a scheme OurBigBook.com
A Zariski sheaf F is a functor represented by a scheme if it has a set of open subfunctors represented by affine schemes whose pullbacks cover every test scheme. The overlaps are open subschemes in both charts, and their identifications satisfy the compatibility on triple overlaps. Gluing of schemes along open subschemes produces a representing scheme; the Zariski sheaf condition identifies its functor of points with F. Conversely, every affine open cover of a scheme supplies such a presentation. A family of local charts covers in this sense without requiring every global element to belong to a single chart.

Open subfunctor (hT​×F​H≅hU​,U⊆T open)

Words: 51
Functor represented by a scheme OurBigBook.com
A subfunctor H⊆F on the opposite of the category of schemes is open if every natural transformation hT​→F pulls it back to a functor represented by a scheme U, with the projection represented by an open immersion U↪T. Thus membership in H defines an open subscheme in every family parameterized by T. This condition is preserved by further pullbacks.

Gluing of schemes along open subschemes

Words: 52
Scheme OurBigBook.com
Given schemes Xi​ and isomorphisms between designated open subschemes satisfying inverse and cocycle conditions, identify the underlying open spaces and glue their structure sheaves. The resulting locally ringed space is locally one of the Xi​, hence a scheme. The same construction works for formal schemes and topological structure sheaves. Compatible morphisms out of the charts glue uniquely.
// Target: ringed-space.bigb

Formal scheme

Words: 161 Articles: 3
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A formal scheme is a locally ringed space with a sheaf of topological rings that is locally a formal spectrum of a complete adic ring. An ordinary scheme is the special case of the discrete topology. A formal completion of a scheme retains all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of a closed subscheme, rather than just that subscheme.
// Target: ringed-space.bigb

Formal completion of a scheme (X/Y​)

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Formal scheme OurBigBook.com
For a closed subscheme with ideal sheaf I in a locally Noetherian scheme, the completion is the formal scheme on ∣Y∣ with topological structure sheaf lim​n​(OX​/In+1)∣∣Y∣​. On a Noetherian affine scheme SpecA, it is Spf(lim​n​A/In+1). Its adic topology remembers every infinitesimal neighbourhood.
// Target: commutative-algebra.bigb
Formal completion commutes with restriction to an open subscheme ((X/Y​)∣U∩Y​≅U/(U∩Y)​)
Words: 41
Formal completion of a scheme OurBigBook.com
Restricting the topological structure sheaf of a formal completion of a scheme to an open subscheme commutes with its inverse limit: both sheaves are lim​n​(OU​/(I∣U​)n+1) on ∣U∩Y∣. Equivalently, the identical infinitesimal neighbourhoods have identical restricted structure sheaves. On formal affine charts this uses completed localization of an adic ring.

Formal spectrum (SpfA)

Words: 43
Formal scheme OurBigBook.com
For a complete ring with an adic topology defined by I, the formal spectrum has the prime ideals containing I as its points and structure sheaf lim​n​OSpec(A/In+1)​. On a principal open subset D(f) its sections form the completed localization of an adic ring, not generally the ordinary localization Af​.

Smooth morphism

Words: 45
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A morphism of schemes is smooth when it is locally of finite presentation, flat and has geometrically regular fibres. Smooth fibres alone do not imply that a morphism is smooth: flatness and the dimension behaviour matter as well. The Abel map of an algebraic curve has smooth projective space fibres whose dimensions can jump.

Étale morphism

Words: 143 Articles: 1
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A morphism of schemes is étale when it is flat, unramified and locally of finite presentation. For a morphism between smooth varieties of the same dimension, an invertible differential gives this property locally. A finite étale morphism over an algebraically closed field has reduced finite fibres, and their cardinalities equal its degree when the source and target are connected.

Finite étale morphism

Words: 88
Étale morphism OurBigBook.com
A finite étale morphism is both a finite morphism and an étale morphism. Affine-locally it is represented by a finite locally free algebra with zero module of Kähler differentials. Its fibres are finite products of finite separable field extensions. For an elliptic curve with good reduction at a prime not dividing m, multiplication by m on its smooth proper group model is finite étale of degree m2: its differential is multiplication by the unit m. A division torsor of a section consequently gives an unramified local extension, the good-prime input to the Weak Mordell-Weil theorem.

Quasi-compact scheme

Words: 29
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme is quasi-compact when its underlying topological space is quasi-compact: every open cover has a finite subcover. Since affine open subsets form a base, this is equivalent to possessing a finite affine open cover. Every affine scheme is quasi-compact.

Open subscheme

Words: 41
Scheme OurBigBook.com
An open subscheme of a scheme X is an open subset U equipped with the restriction of its structure sheaf. Its inclusion is an open immersion. Every scheme is covered by affine open subschemes. Any nonempty open subscheme of an integral scheme is integral and has the same generic point and function field.

Irreducible scheme

Words: 29
Scheme OurBigBook.com
An irreducible scheme is one whose underlying topological space is a nonempty irreducible topological space. It can have nilpotent elements in its structure sheaf; irreducibility concerns only the topology. A reduced scheme is an integral scheme precisely when it is irreducible.

Dimension of a scheme (dimX)

Words: 41
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets of its underlying topological space. On an affine scheme it is the Krull dimension of its coordinate ring. Taking the reduced subscheme leaves the dimension unchanged.

Structure morphism (X→SpecZ)

Words: 30
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The structure morphism of a scheme X is its unique morphism X→SpecZ. More generally, an S-scheme comes equipped with a specified morphism to the base scheme S.

Scheme of characteristic p (charX=p)

Words: 192 Articles: 2
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme X has characteristic p when p⋅1=0 in its structure sheaf of a scheme. Equivalently, its structure morphism X→SpecZ factors through SpecFp​.

Absolute Frobenius morphism (FX​:X→X)

Words: 173 Articles: 1
Scheme of characteristic p OurBigBook.com
The absolute Frobenius morphism of a scheme of characteristic p is the identity on the underlying topological space and raises every local function to its pth power. On an affine chart SpecA it is induced contravariantly by the Frobenius endomorphism A→A, a↦ap. It need not be an isomorphism of schemes, even when it acts invertibly on global sections.
The algebraic Frobenius endomorphism induces this scheme map contravariantly on affine charts.
Frobenius factorization through a finite normal cover (Lp⊆KorK⊆Lp)
Words: 108
Absolute Frobenius morphism OurBigBook.com
For a finite surjective map of normal integral schemes with function fields K⊆L in characteristic p, the condition Lp⊆K lets the Absolute Frobenius morphism of the source factor through the map. On an affine chart A⊆B, send b to bp∈A: it lies in K, is integral over A, and A is integrally closed. The condition K⊆Lp instead lets the map factor after the source Frobenius. Send a to its unique pth root in L; that root lies in the normal ring B because it satisfies a monic polynomial over B. These rules localize and glue; injectivity of Frobenius in the function field supplies uniqueness.

Structure sheaf of a scheme (OX​)

Words: 525 Articles: 8
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The structure sheaf OX​ records the regular functions on every open subset of a scheme X. Its stalk OX,x​ is the local ring of functions defined near x.

Nilradical sheaf (NX​)

Words: 71
Structure sheaf of a scheme OurBigBook.com
The nilradical sheaf of a scheme is the ideal sheaf of locally nilpotent sections in its structure sheaf. On an affine open subscheme SpecA it is the quasi-coherent sheaf associated to the nilradical of A, since the nilradical commutes with localization. Its quotient defines the reduced induced subscheme. On a Noetherian scheme it has a uniform nilpotence exponent: take nilpotence bounds on a finite affine open cover and use their maximum. On a general scheme, a locally nilpotent section need not have a single nilpotence exponent over a non-quasi-compact open subset.

Idempotent–clopen correspondence (e⟷D(e)=V(1−e))

Words: 70
Structure sheaf of a scheme OurBigBook.com
A global idempotent on a scheme is zero or one in every local ring. Its one-locus is both open and closed. Conversely a clopen subset determines a global idempotent by gluing one on it and zero on its complement. Under this correspondence, decompositions into nonzero orthogonal idempotents correspond to disjoint clopen decompositions. When all connected components are open, the primitive idempotents correspond exactly to those components. Without orthogonality the assertion fails in characteristic two: (1,0)=(1,1)+(0,1) in F2​×F2​.

Sheaf of units of the structure sheaf (OX∗​)

Words: 35
Structure sheaf of a scheme OurBigBook.com
The units in the structure sheaf of a scheme form a multiplicative sheaf of abelian groups. On a smooth algebraic curve, a nonzero rational function is a unit at a point precisely when its discrete valuation there is zero. Its inclusion in the sheaf of nonzero rational functions on an irreducible variety relates divisor on an algebraic curve to the Picard group through the long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology.

Regular function

Words: 320 Articles: 4
Structure sheaf of a scheme OurBigBook.com
A regular function on an open subset U of a scheme X is a section of OX​(U). On an affine variety it is locally a quotient of polynomial functions with a denominator that does not vanish.
On a variety, a regular function is a regular map to the affine line; the arbitrary-target regular-map concept is broader.
Global regular function (f∈Γ(X,OX​))
Words: 266 Articles: 3
Regular function OurBigBook.com
A global regular function is a global section of the structure sheaf of a scheme, defined on the entire scheme. These functions form its ring H0(X,OX​). On an affine scheme this recovers the defining ring; on a positive-dimensional projective complete intersection it consists only of constants over the base field.
Denominator ideal proof for global regular functions
Words: 97
Global regular function OurBigBook.com
A regular function f on an entire affine variety is a polynomial function, even if the variety is reducible. Put J={g∈A(X):gf∈A(X)}, an ideal of its coordinate ring. Near a point p, write f=a/b with b nonzero, and choose a principal open subset D(h) containing p inside that neighbourhood. Then (hb)f=ha on all of X: on D(h) this is the fraction identity, and off D(h) both sides vanish. Hence hb∈J and (hb)(p)=0. No point is a common zero of J, so the weak Hilbert Nullstellensatz implies J=A(X). Thus 1∈J and f∈A(X). This proof does not require a fraction field for a reducible coordinate ring.
Global regular functions on an irreducible projective variety (H0(X,OX​)=k)
Words: 67
Global regular function OurBigBook.com
Over an algebraically closed field, every regular function on a nonempty irreducible projective variety is constant. Regard the function as a morphism to P1 avoiding infinity. Its graph is closed; the closedness of projection from projective space makes its image closed in P1. A proper closed subset there is finite, and an irreducible finite image is a singleton. Irreducibility is the usual variety convention; on a disconnected projective algebraic set different components may have different constants.
Regular functions on the punctured affine plane
Words: 59
Global regular function OurBigBook.com
For W=Ak2​∖{0}, restriction to D(x) and D(y) gives
Γ(W,OW​)=k[x,y]x​∩k[x,y]y​=k[x,y].
(1)
The intersection is taken in k(x,y) and the equality follows from unique factorization: a reduced denominator dividing powers of both x and y is a unit. The inclusion W↪A2 induces an isomorphism on global functions but is not an isomorphism, so W is not an affine variety.

Reduced scheme

Words: 156 Articles: 3
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme is reduced when every local ring OX,x​ is a reduced ring, equivalently when its structure sheaf has no nonzero nilpotent element. The affine scheme SpecA is reduced exactly when A is reduced.

Generic reducedness with no embedded components

Words: 45
Reduced scheme OurBigBook.com
A Noetherian scheme with no embedded associated primes is reduced if it is reduced at all its generic points. Locally, a nonzero nilpotent ideal would have an associated prime, necessarily a minimal prime. Its localization there would be nonzero, contradicting generic reducedness. This is useful with the unmixedness of a complete intersection.

Integral scheme

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Reduced scheme OurBigBook.com
An integral scheme is a nonempty scheme that is both reduced and irreducible. An affine scheme SpecA is integral exactly when A is an integral domain.
Generic-point embedding of regular functions (Γ(U,OX​)↪K(X))
Words: 55
Integral scheme OurBigBook.com
On an integral scheme X, every nonempty open U contains its generic point η. Taking a germ gives an injective ring homomorphism from its regular functions to the function field OX,η​. Injectivity follows on each nonempty affine open subscheme from the injection of an integral domain into its field of fractions, and then from the sheaf gluing axiom. This lets regular functions on different open subsets be compared inside one field.

Group scheme

Words: 94 Articles: 2
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A group scheme over a base scheme S is an S-scheme G with multiplication m:G×S​G→G, an identity section e:S→G, and inversion i:G→G satisfying the group axioms as equalities of morphisms.

Homomorphism of group schemes

Words: 28
Group scheme OurBigBook.com
A homomorphism of group schemes f:H→G is a morphism over the base that commutes with multiplication: f∘mH​=mG​∘(f×f). It consequently preserves the identity and inversion.

Multiplication-by-n morphism ([n]G​)

Words: 30
Group scheme OurBigBook.com
For a commutative group scheme G, the multiplication-by-n morphism [n]G​:G→G adds a point to itself n times. On an abelian variety, it is surjective for every nonzero integer n.

Nonreduced scheme

Words: 68 Articles: 1
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme is nonreduced when its structure sheaf contains a nonzero nilpotent element. For an affine scheme Spec(A/I), this is equivalent to the ideal I not being radical.

Nonreduced double point (Speck[ϵ]/(ϵ2))

Words: 40
Nonreduced scheme OurBigBook.com
The spectrum of the dual number ring k[ϵ]/(ϵ2) is a nonreduced scheme of length two supported at one point. Its nonzero nilpotent ϵ retains first-order information that the underlying singleton topological space forgets. It differs from the disjoint union of two reduced k-points.

Punctual scheme

Words: 30
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme over an algebraically closed field is punctual when its underlying topological space consists of one closed rational point. It may have nontrivial nilpotent structure, such as Speck[ε]/(ε2).

Spectrum of a commutative ring (SpecA)

Words: 1k Articles: 21
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The spectrum SpecA of a commutative ring A is the set of its prime ideals, with closed sets V(I)={p:I⊆p} and a structure sheaf whose sections locally look like fractions.

Spectrum map for the complexification of a real polynomial ring (SpecC[x]→SpecR[x])

Words: 52
Spectrum of a commutative ring OurBigBook.com
Contraction sends the zero prime ideal to zero. A complex closed point (x−z) contracts to (x−z) when z is real, and to ((x−Rez)2+(Imz)2) otherwise. Thus the map on the spectrum of a commutative ring is surjective and identifies each nonreal conjugate pair. Both spectra have only finite proper Zariski-closed sets, so this is also the topological quotient by complex conjugation.

0⟶OPn​(−d)⋅fd​​OPn​⟶i∗​OX​⟶0.

Reduced induced subscheme
Words: 30
Closed subscheme OurBigBook.com
Every closed subset Z⊆X has a canonical reduced closed-subscheme structure defined affine-locally by Spec(A/I​) when Z=V(I)⊆SpecA. It is the smallest closed subscheme with underlying set Z.
Scheme-theoretic image
Words: 57
Closed subscheme OurBigBook.com
The scheme-theoretic image of f:X→Y is the smallest closed subscheme of Y through which f factors. For an affine morphism SpecB→SpecA induced by φ:A→B, it is Spec(A/kerφ), whose underlying set is the closure of the set-theoretic image.
The construction retains the scheme structure on the closed subscheme, not merely the set of points in an image.

Affine plane with doubled origin

Words: 63
Scheme OurBigBook.com
The affine plane with doubled origin is formed by gluing two copies of Ak2​ by the identity away from the origin. The overlap is the punctured affine plane, so this scheme is nonseparated and the two-open affine cover is not acyclic for the structure sheaf.
The gluing resembles a non-Hausdorff manifold example, but this node concerns an algebraic scheme and its nonseparatedness, not a real manifold.

Semi-separated scheme

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Scheme OurBigBook.com
A scheme is semi-separated when the intersection of any two affine open subsets is affine, equivalently when its diagonal is affine. This condition makes affine covers acyclic for quasi-coherent sheaves.

Exact direct image from an affine open in a semi-separated scheme (j∗​:QCoh(U)→QCoh(X))

Words: 50
Semi-separated scheme OurBigBook.com
If U is an affine open subscheme of a semi-separated scheme, its open immersion j:U↪X has exact direct image on quasi-coherent sheaves. Test on an affine open V of X: the intersection U∩V is affine, and the affine module-sheaf equivalence makes sections on this intersection exact. The direct image is also quasi-coherent, since this open immersion is an affine morphism.
